draft.title: Context and values in paired texts
card: Context is the time, place and society in which a text is made. It includes the beliefs and events that shaped the composer.
Values are the beliefs about what is right, important or normal that a text promotes or questions. Different contexts often hold different values.
When two texts share a story but come from different times, the same character or idea can be treated in different ways. Comparing the contexts can explain why.
To compare, name what each text does with the shared element. Then link each choice to the values of its own time, rather than judging one text as better.
draft.remember: Different times hold different values, and these help explain why a shared story is told differently.

a.q: Why compare the contexts of two texts that share a story?
opts: It can explain why each treats the story differently
It proves the later text is better than the earlier
It shows the composers must have known each other
It shows that both texts hold the same values
a.why: Contexts shape the values a composer holds, so they help explain different treatments of the same story. Judging one text better is wrong, because the aim is to explain the differences, not rank the texts.
a.clue: Think about what shapes a composer's choices.

b.q: An old tale casts a stepmother as a plain villain. A modern retelling shows her as a worried widow who is under pressure. What best explains the change?
opts: The later context values complex, sympathetic characters
The later composer misread the original tale
The earlier context had no values about families
The later text is simply a more accurate version
b.why: The shift shows that the later context values understanding characters, not just sorting them into good and bad. The idea of a more accurate version is tempting, but a retelling is shaped by its own values, not by correcting a true account.
b.clue: Link the change in the character to the values of the later time.

a.best: It can explain why each treats the story differently

b.best: The later context values complex, sympathetic characters
